page: Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-160 is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. It features 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 3844 GB RAM, translating to approximately 24.02 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics falling into the bottom 10%. However, the massive core count enables strong multi-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, scoring in the top 25% for both cached and uncached large-block read operations. This high memory throughput supports rapid data access, as evidenced by strong Redis SET operations exceeding 79 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a specialized hardware profile where budget is allocated heavily toward memory density rather than raw single-core compute speed or local storage. The lack of bundled local storage means external storage solutions must be provisioned separately. The primary trade-off is the lower clock speed of 2.2 GHz and lack of AVX-512 vector extensions, which limits its suitability for compute-bound or single-threaded tasks.

The m1-ultramem-160 is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive caching layers, and heavy data warehousing operations. It is also appropriate for high-throughput static web serving and multi-threaded data processing tasks that can leverage its 160 vCPUs and extensive memory footprint, whereas it is poorly suited for single-threaded applications or GPU-dependent machine learning training.
